problem:
Given that

$$
\begin{aligned}L{\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t}=\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+{\omega }^{2}}, &  & s>0 \\ L{{t}^{n}}=\frac{n!}{{s}^{n+1}}, &  & s>0,\end{aligned}
$$

find the Laplace transform of  $f(t)=3-\operatorname{cos}⁡3t$ for $s>0.$
worked_solution:
The linearity property of the Laplace transform states that for functions $f(t)$ and $g(t),$ we have

$$
L{\alpha f(t)+\beta g(t)}=\alpha \cdot L{f(t)}+\beta \cdot L{g(t)}
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants.

Taking the Laplace transform and applying the linearity properties, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{f(t)} & =L{3-\operatorname{cos}⁡3t} \\  & =L{3}-L{\operatorname{cos}⁡3t} \\  & =3L{1}-L{\operatorname{cos}⁡3t}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're given that 

$$
L{\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t}=\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+{\omega }^{2}},\,L{{t}^{n}}=\frac{n!}{{s}^{n+1}}.
$$

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{1} & =\frac{1}{s},\,s>0 \\ L{\operatorname{cos}⁡3t} & =\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+9},\,s>0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Laplace transform of $f(t)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}L{f(t)} & =3L{1}-L{\operatorname{cos}⁡3t} \\  & =3\cdot \frac{1}{s}-\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+9} \\  & =\frac{3({s}^{2}+9)-{s}^{2}}{s({s}^{2}+9)} \\  & =\frac{3{s}^{2}+27-{s}^{2}}{s({s}^{2}+9)} \\  & =\frac{2{s}^{2}+27}{s({s}^{2}+9)},\,s>0.\end{aligned}
$$
